context.why: The organization half of profile editing. US1 is accepted on this branch: Contributor.is_editable_by (base False, Person override), LinesField and PersonProfileForm in forms/profile.py, the Update page in plugins/update.py with its shipped_forms map and FAIRDM_PROFILE_FORMS fallback, the person overview wiring, and the docs. This story adds the organization form, the parent loop guard on the model, who keeps an organization, the organization overview wiring, development data, and one robustness fix shared by both forms (T018). Community managers come in US3.
prior_decisions: decisions.md D2, D3, D5, D6, D10, and the entries US1 wrote (D11 onward). Read those entries.
Organization.is_editable_by in this story: is_managed_by(user) and the user is active. No superuser bypass, no community manager yet.

Website and links (D5): the form's `website` and `links` fields are read from and written to the stored `links` list, website first, no repeats. Clearing the website makes the next link the website on reopening: do not write a test that expects an empty website field after that.

The loop guard goes in Organization.clean, keyed to the `parent` field, using a new Organization.get_descendant_ids(). The form's parent field offers organizations and reports the refusal on the field with the reason.

Parent picker: use an organization-select widget the package already has if one fits (look in fairdm/contrib/contributors/forms/widgets.py and fairdm/contrib/autocomplete), otherwise a plain select, and note which in decisions.md.

A deactivated administrator is signed out by Django (ModelBackend.get_user), so a page test of one expects the redirect to sign in. The model-level test of is_editable_by with an inactive user still expects False.

Organization overview: when can_manage, the menu's 'Edit details' entry becomes a working link and the other two entries stay disabled. Pass `can_edit` and `update_url` in the context as the person page does. The single edit button for an editor who does not keep the record is US3's.
Update.page_title: 'Edit organization' for an organization. Update.shipped_forms gains the organization form.

T018: Django's model form raises ValueError when Model.clean raises an error keyed to a field the form lacks. Fix it once in a shared base for the two profile forms (override _post_clean or _update_errors so such errors become non-field errors), test first, for both forms.

Seed accounts in seed_profiles follow the existing example_accounts pattern in demo/seed/common.py: addresses at example.com, password `password`. Use admin.user@example.com for the administrator, member.user@example.com for the member, former-admin.user@example.com for the ended administrator, on the organization regular.user@example.com owns. If fairdm.E501 or EXAMPLE_ACCOUNT_EMAILS in fairdm/management/commands/create_dev_accounts.py needs to know these addresses, add them there.

acceptance.given_when_then: Given the organization shapes and users in tasks.md T007, when the model methods and full_clean are called, then descendants, the loop refusal and is_editable_by behave as listed.
Given OrganizationProfileForm, when bound with the cases in tasks.md T008, then fields, website/links round trip, required name, list choices and parent refusals behave as listed.
Given US-2 scenarios 2 to 6 and 8 to 11, when the real page is opened and submitted as each kind of user, then each Then holds and refused requests store nothing.

Given an owner, an administrator, a member and a stranger on the organization overview, when it renders, then the menu's edit entry and the five checklist items link as tasks.md T010 lists and nobody else is offered an edit link.
Given the failing tests from T007 to T010, when the implementation lands, then all pass with no migration.
Given a development environment, when seed_profiles runs, then the three new accounts exist with their affiliations, the seed test covers them, and the docs step passes.

Given a stored person or organization that fails model validation on a field the form lacks, when the form is submitted, then it is invalid with a form-level error and nothing is saved, instead of raising.
